paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the performance of various knowledge editing methods on BioMedLM, with accuracy (ACC %) on the y-axis and co-occurrence number on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 1 to 10³. The "Base" model, represented by a black line with circular markers, starts at approximately 39% accuracy and gradually increases to around 44%, showing the lowest performance across all co-occurrence frequencies. The FT method, shown in blue with triangle markers, begins at about 40% and rises to roughly 48%, exhibiting steady improvement. The IKE method, in red with inverted triangle markers, starts at approximately 43% and climbs to about 50%, surpassing FT at co-occurrence numbers above 10². MEND, depicted in brown with square markers, begins at around 44% and reaches approximately 56%, showing strong performance. MEMIT, in purple with pentagon markers, starts at about 43% and increases to roughly 55%. ROME, represented by a green line with square markers, demonstrates the highest performance, starting at approximately 51% and rising to about 66% at the highest co-occurrence number, consistently outperforming all other methods.
